title: Batching & Cache Tuner incident retrospective and safe-apply playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Post-incident retrospective for the Optimize autotuner rollout that briefly increased 95th/99th tail latency and caused service-level errors for a subset of high-concurrency customers. This ticket captures timeline, root causes, immediate mitigations, and a concrete safe-apply / rollback playbook to prevent recurrence.
incident_summary: On 2026-02-17 an autotuner job pushed a new batching + KV-cache policy to the hosted pool without sufficient staged validation. The config increased batching window and enabled aggressive KV prefetching which produced higher memory pressure on a small set of instances and a regression in tail latency for requests with long context windows. Several enterprise customers experienced elevated error rates and degraded p95/p99 latency for ~28 minutes before automated rollback and manual throttles restored baseline behavior.
timeline: 2026-02-17T12:02Z - Autotune job scheduled and began staged rollout to 5% of requests in hosted cluster
2026-02-17T12:12Z - Observability alerts triggered: p99 latency +400ms on region us-west-2; error rate for model/gptx-1-14 spiked from 0.1% to 2.9%
2026-02-17T12:14Z - On-call alerted; initial hypothesis: change in batching heuristics increasing queueing latency
2026-02-17T12:18Z - Canary traffic throttled to 0% via rollout controller; autotuner apply paused
2026-02-17T12:25Z - Investigations revealed increased memory churn on runtime instances leading to GC pauses (long-lived tensors from prefetching + larger batch allocs)
2026-02-17T12:35Z - Automated safety policy triggered full rollback (config rollback path); traffic gradually recovered
2026-02-17T12:50Z - Incident declared resolved; post-incident assessment started
root_causes: Insufficient canary workload fidelity: the canary traffic profile did not include long-context requests that revealed the memory regression
Autotuner permitted multi-dimensional config changes (batch window + cache prefetching) in a single rollout without atomic validation for each axis
No automatic SLO-regression abort threshold for memory/GC pause metrics — rollout controller primarily watched tail latency and errors but not heap churn and GC duration
Runtime had a latent interaction: enabling aggressive KV prefetch plus increased batch window amplified transient memory spikes causing GC-induced tail latency
immediate_actions: Manual pause of autotuner job and cancellation of pending apply tasks
Full automatic rollback executed by rollout controller (restore last known-good config)
Critical alert: created a short-lived runtime throttle for affected tenants to reduce concurrency on vulnerable instance shapes
Added ephemeral dashboards for heap allocation, GC pause time, and batch allocation rate to the incident channel
long_term_mitigations: Split autotuner changes into orthogonal dimensions and require per-dimension dry-run validation (batching, prefetching, quantization) before combinatorial apply
Enhance canary harness to synthesize long-context, high-concurrency request shapes (multi-tenant replay + stress tests)
Add memory and GC pause metrics to automated SLO regression checks; rollout abort if any of these exceed configured thresholds
Implement a staged apply that progressively widens scope only after passing a fixed set of resource-containment checks (heap, swap, GC) for N minutes
Introduce per-tenant ‘safety fences’ so heavy-optimizations are blocked for customers with strict latency SLOs unless explicitly approved
Store every autotuner candidate config with a reproducible dry-run artifact and a checksum to enable deterministic rollback and fast forensic replay
playbook_steps: Detection: Alerts for p95/p99 latency or error rate + memory/Gc pause exceedance route to on-call and SRE
Triage: Confirm rollouts in last 60m via autotuner audit log; identify candidate config hashes
Contain: If rollout is active, call rollout-controller pause endpoint and scale down canary to 0% immediately
Rollback: Trigger config rollback using the stored last-known-good checksum. Verify runtime config hash matches expected stable state
Throttle: If rollback incomplete, apply per-tenant concurrency throttle to protect exposed customers
Verify: Run synthetic replay of failing request shapes against rolled-back config and monitor heap/Gc/latency windows for 30 minutes
Postmortem: Open retrospective doc; assign owners and due dates for mitigations within 72 hours
rollback_criteria: Immediate abort if p99 latency increases >30% relative to baseline for >5 minutes
Immediate abort if error rate increases above 1% absolute (or 3x baseline) for >3 minutes
Abort if GC pause time median or 95th percentile increases >50ms relative to baseline for >5 minutes
Abort if heap allocation rate per-second increases >2x baseline sustained for >60s
automation_requirements: Rollout controller: support multi-axis staged rollouts and per-metric aborts (latency, errors, heap, GC)
Autotuner: emit explainability metadata for each param change and include a dry-run outcome summary
CI/dry-run harness: integrate a resource-stress mode that reproduces long-context request shapes and variable concurrency
Audit trail: ensure every apply has a unique config-id, owner, and linkable dry-run artifact; store in central config registry
